chunks: May Allah have mercy on a man who ponders and takes lesson thereby,
and when he takes lesson he achieves enlightenment. Whatever is present in this world would shortly not exist, while whatever is to exist in the next world is already in existence.
Every countable thing would pass away. Every anticipation should be taken to be coming up and everything that is to come up should be taken as just near.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of pondering the transient nature of the world versus the permanence of the Hereafter in Shia spirituality?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) presents a psychological framework for spiritual awakening, where deep contemplation (tafakkur) leads to insight (absar), effectively detaching the believer from the transient world while anchoring them in the eternal Hereafter. This passage is central to the Shia concept of *zuhd* (asceticism), not as mere renunciation, but as a cognitive shift that makes the future reality feel more immediate than the present moment. The concluding triad of certainties—everything counted ends, everything expected arrives, and everything arriving is near—serves as a reminder of the inevitability of divine decree and the urgency of preparation.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Allāh may shower His mercy on him who ponders and takes lesson thereby,
and when he takes lesson he achieves enlightenment. Whatever is present in this world would shortly not exist, while whatever is to exist in the next world is already in existence.
Every countable thing would pass away. Every anticipation should be taken to be coming up and everything that is to come up should be taken as just near.
